Placeholder overview: review `README.md` and `/src` to determine repository purpose and structure, then update this overview.

**Framework:** .NET 10.0 (`net10.0`); latest C#; nullable reference types and implicit usings enabled; warnings treated as errors globally.
Structure: `src/` production projects, `tests/` test projects, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `Template.slnx`.

**Packages:** MSBuild Central Package Management (`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true`). All versions are in [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props); project `.csproj` references omit versions. To add a package, add `<PackageVersion Include="PackageName" Version="x.y.z" />` there. All projects inherit [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props). Warning 1591 (missing XML comments) is suppressed via `NoWarn`.

**C# style:** Prefer file-scoped `namespace MyProject.Feature;` (warning if not used); avoid block namespaces. Private fields use `_camelCase`; constants PascalCase; use `var` for built-in or apparent types. Interfaces use `I`; async methods end in `Async`. Use braces except for single-line exits (`return`, `throw`); Allman braces, 2-space indentation, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM. File-scoped namespace directives go outside namespace. Prefer primary constructors; ALWAYS assign to readonly fields. Prefer top-level statements, pattern matching, and expression-bodied properties/indexers/accessors (NOT methods). Run `dotnet format`; use analyzers in [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props). Consider NSDepCop.

**Configuration/logging:** Use `appsettings.json` and `appsettings.{Environment}.json`, `IConfiguration`/`IOptions<T>`, strongly typed classes for complex settings, and User Secrets for development. Never hardcode sensitive information in source code. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, appropriate levels, contextual structured logs, and correlation IDs when possible; avoid logging sensitive information.

**Validation/security:** Use `Ardalis.GuardClauses` for non-UI input validation; prefer `FluentValidation` for complex scenarios, especially UI. Invalid UI input should produce user-friendly errors, not exceptions; invalid non-UI input should throw appropriate guard-clause exceptions. HTTP methods should return suitable non-success status codes (e.g., 400 Bad Request). Follow OWASP; validate and sanitize all user input; use parameterized queries or ORM features to prevent SQL injection; implement proper authentication and authorization; use HTTPS for all communications.

**Design:** Write unit-testable code; offer tests for generated code if applicable, in `tests/`. Only test code you control with business logic; do not test framework code. Keep classes single-responsibility, use DI, favor composition, async/await for I/O, short focused methods (ideally under 20 lines), and short argument lists (consider parameter objects beyond 4). Prefer FastEndpoints REPR; apply DDD where appropriate. API messages: `*Request`/`*Response`; use-case messages: `*Command`/`*Query`; use DTOs between layers, not exposed domain entities; DTO suffixes `*Details`/`*Summary` as appropriate. Avoid locating interfaces and implementations in the same project.

**Projects/tests:** Production projects belong in `src/`, test projects in `tests/`; test projects should use `xUnit`. Use `xUnit` for all tests. Run: `dotnet run --project src/YourProject/YourProject.csproj`. Use Arrange-Act-Assert with whitespace separation, no comments. Organize tests by feature in folders mirroring `src/`. Do not name test classes with "Tests" suffix; do use "Tests" suffix for folders if needed. Example: `ProductServiceTests/ProductService_Constructor.cs`. Name test classes `ClassName_MethodName.cs`, methods `DoesSomething_GivenSomeCondition`; together, names should form a sentence describing the use case. Example: `ProductService_Constructor._ReturnsInstanceGivenValidInputs`. Separate unit and integration tests into projects or folders. Prefer NSubstitute for mocking and Shouldly for assertions; avoid commercially licensed testing libraries (e.g. FluentAssertions, Moq).

**Documentation:** Use Markdown, headings, syntax-highlighted snippets, and lint documentation. Lists and code listings should have a blank line before and after.

References: [.editorconfig](.editorconfig) (code style); [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props) (build/compiler settings); [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props) (package versions); [.gitignore](.gitignore) (Visual Studio patterns).
